rv.q: The thrilling new revival of Stephen Sondheim and Hugh Wheeler's 'Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street' burrows into your thoughts with the poisoned seductiveness of a campfire storyteller who knows what really scares you.
Stephen Sondheim's masterwork is lifted high in unexpected ways in an audacious reinterpretation.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actor in a Musical

aw.sub: Won Best Direction of a Musical + 1 more

cn.t: This audacious reinterpretation lifts Sondheim's masterwork to fresh heights, delivering one of Broadway's most beguiling productions in recent memory with an unexpected approach that reinvigorates the classic.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
